title: How much property tax do cities collect?
summary: The same 28 cities, compared by property-tax receipts as a share of property value and city revenue. Prague’s 0.45% is an illustrative peer-median scenario, not a measured Prague tax rate.
methodology:
Working draft for human review, based on the comparison prepared on 20 September 2026. U.S. receipts refer to FY2024; Rotterdam to 2024; Amsterdam, Santiago and Prague revenue to 2025. Numerators are city-government receipts: separately governed school, county and district taxes are excluded. Santiago uses the municipality’s retained receipts.

Property denominators differ: official market/full values, taxable assessed values and approximate values reconstructed from debt ratios. Assessed values may differ materially from current market prices; this is not a like-for-like homeowner tax-bill ranking. Verify each denominator and fiscal-year alignment before publication, especially Mesa (2024 assessment roll), Phoenix and the California cities.

Prague: 0.450363% is the unweighted median of the other 27 rows. It is an illustrative scenario, not an estimate based on Prague property values. Prague’s measured revenue share remains 1.837324%. Austin’s tax numerator is Census-imputed. Source links and row notes must be reviewed by the publishing author.
